issue.title: Fix Pylint 2.0 violations

labels.name: ack
labels.description: Pull Request approved, can be merged

labels.name: pushed
labels.description: Pull Request has already been pushed

repository.name: freeipa
repository.description: Mirror of FreeIPA, an integrated security information management solution

issue.body:
Fix the following violations aiming to support Pylint 2.0

- `unneeded-not` (C0113):
  Consider changing "not item in items" to "item not in items" used
  when a boolean expression contains an unneeded negation.

- `useless-import-alias` (C0414):
  Import alias does not rename original package Used when an import
  alias is same as original package.e.g using import numpy as numpy
  instead of import numpy as np

- `raising-format-tuple` (W0715):
  Exception arguments suggest string formatting might be intended Used
  when passing multiple arguments to an exception constructor, the
  first of them a string literal containing what appears to be
  placeholders intended for formatting

- `bad-continuation` (C0330):
  This was already included on the disable list, although with current
  version of pylint (2.0.0.dev2) violations at the end of the files
  are not being ignored.
  See: PyCQA/pylint#2278

- `try-except-raise` (E0705):
  The except handler raises immediately Used when an except handler
  uses raise as its first or only operator. This is useless because it
  raises back the exception immediately. Remove the raise operator or
  the entire try-except-raise block!

- `consider-using-set-comprehension` (R1718):
  Consider using a set comprehension Although there is nothing
  syntactically wrong with this code, it is hard to read and can be
  simplified to a set comprehension.Also it is faster since you don't
  need to create another transient list

- `dict-keys-not-iterating` (W1655):
  dict.keys referenced when not iterating Used when dict.keys is
  referenced in a non-iterating context (returns an iterator in
  Python 3)

- `comprehension-escape` (W1662):
  Using a variable that was bound inside a comprehension Emitted when
  using a variable, that was bound in a comprehension handler, outside
  of the comprehension itself. On Python 3 these variables will be
  deleted outside of the comprehension.

Issue: https://pagure.io/freeipa/issue/7614

Signed-off-by: Armando Neto <abiagion@redhat.com>

body: Can confirm. Thanks for the report

body:
Notes:

* ~~`astroid` node `.tolineno` and `.fromlineno` counts starting from zero~~
* tokenizer `TokenInfo` class line `start` attribute counts starting from 1 (excluding the encoding token)
* pylint reports line number starting from 1
* astroid tolineno and fromlineno count starting from 1, but tolineno isn't always accurate

~This causes some fun off by one errors all over the place when using `add_message` with tokenizer checkers, and makes add_message think the line is past the end of the file and auto enabling the message for some ast corner case~

~I think the best solution is to add by one in the case of astroid `line=node.tolineno`/fromlineno so users get the correct line number, keep tokenizer line report values the same, and then consider one based indexing in `add_message` so that the last line isn't ignored + document~

issue.title: Cannot disable trailing-newlines with --disable=C,R

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
Given a python file (file.py):
```
""" Example: Note spaces and empty lines. """
print("Hello world!")  



```

Running pylint file.py yields:
```
C:\Users\username\Desktop>pylint file.py
************* Module file
file.py:2:21: C0303: Trailing whitespace (trailing-whitespace)
file.py:3:0: C0305: Trailing newlines (trailing-newlines)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
Your code has been rated at -10.00/10 (previous run: -10.00/10, +0.00)
```
(Second note: Why does it give a -10 score when 0 is expected?)

:
Running with --disable=R,C should remove both convention errors but i get the following result:
```
C:\Users\username\Desktop>pylint --disable=R,C file.py
************* Module file
file.py:3:0: C0305: Trailing newlines (trailing-newlines)

---------------------------------------------------------------------
Your code has been rated at 0.00/10 (previous run: -10.00/10, +10.00)
```
Pylint 1.9.0 works as intended giving no errors while Pylint 2.0.0 returns C0305 as an error.
